## Description

Primary source:

<https://ngs101.com/how-to-analyze-single-cell-rna-seq-data-complete-beginners-guide-part-7-trajectory-and-pseudotime-analysis-using-monocle-3/>

Part 3 of 3. The pseudotime ordering from part 2 is checked against biology:
pseudotime per cell type and partition, known marker genes, and a test for
differences between conditions. `graph_test()` (Moran's I on the principal
graph) then finds genes whose expression varies along the trajectory, and
pseudotime is added back to the Seurat object.

`graph_test()` runs on every gene in the CDS and is slow; use
`params$graphtest.cores` to parallelize it.

Code is taken from the source article's code blocks (steps 13-19 and the
"common pitfalls" snippets). Changes made for this notebook series: hard-coded
values moved into the YAML front matter, paths built from `params` rather than
`setwd()`, and changes marked `ADDED:` or `FIX:` in comments.

## Libraries and directories

```{r step1_libs_data}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 1: Load required libraries
#-----------------------------------------------

# Core single-cell analysis
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)
library(SeuratWrappers)

# Trajectory inference
library(monocle3)

# Data manipulation and visualization
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(viridis)

source(here::here("helper_functions", "params_read.R"))
params <- params_ingest()

# Set working directory
base.dir <- params$base.dir
traj.dir <- file.path(base.dir, params$traj.subdir)

# Create output directories
for (d in c("plots/pseudotime", "plots/genes_over_pseudotime", "results")) {
  if (!dir.exists(file.path(traj.dir, d))) dir.create(file.path(traj.dir, d), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Set random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(params$seed)

# Configure plotting defaults
theme_set(theme_classic(base_size = 12))

celltype.col <- params$celltype.col
condition.col <- params$condition.col
```

## Load objects from parts 1-2

```{r step2_load_obj}
# ADDED: hand-off from parts 1-2
seurat_subset <- readRDS(file.path(traj.dir, "results/seurat_subset_downsampled.rds"))
cds_main <- readRDS(file.path(traj.dir, "results/cds_main_ordered.rds"))
plot_data <- readRDS(file.path(traj.dir, "results/plot_data.rds"))
load(file.path(traj.dir, "results/traj_part1.RData")) # umap_reduction

cat("CDS: ", ncol(cds_main), " cells; partitions: ",
    paste(levels(factor(partitions(cds_main))), collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
```

## Biological validation: does the trajectory make sense?

Pseudotime is only comparable within a partition, so cell types are summarized
per partition.

```{r step3_pseudotime_summary}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 13: Validation - trajectory structure per partition
#-----------------------------------------------

# Count cells in each cell type along pseudotime
# Group by partition for proper interpretation
pseudotime_summary <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(partition, cell_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n_cells = n(),
    median_pseudotime = median(pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_pseudotime = min(pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_pseudotime = max(pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(partition, median_pseudotime)

cat("Pseudotime summary by cell type and partition:\n")
print(as.data.frame(pseudotime_summary))
```

### Marker genes along the trajectory

Naive T cell markers (CCR7, LEF1, TCF7) should decrease along a T cell
trajectory and activation markers (CD69, HLA-DRA, IL2RA) should increase.

```{r step4_marker_genes, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 14: Validation - marker gene expression
#-----------------------------------------------

# Test known markers along pseudotime
marker_genes <- unlist(params$marker.genes)

# Check if markers are in dataset
marker_genes <- marker_genes[marker_genes %in% rownames(cds_main)]

if (length(marker_genes) > 0) {
  # Plot each marker along pseudotime
  for (gene in marker_genes) {
    p <- plot_cells(
      cds_main,
      genes = gene,
      label_cell_groups = FALSE,
      show_trajectory_graph = TRUE,
      cell_size = 1
    ) +
      scale_color_viridis(option = "magma", name = "Expression") +
      ggtitle(paste0("Expression of ", gene, " Along Trajectory"))
    print(p)

    ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, paste0("plots/genes_over_pseudotime/marker_", gene, ".png")),
           p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
  }
  cat("Saved marker gene trajectory plots\n")
} else {
  cat("Marker genes not found in dataset\n")
}
```

### Condition effects

```{r step5_condition_effects}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 15: Validation - condition effects
#-----------------------------------------------

# Statistical test: Do conditions differ in pseudotime distribution?
# (pseudotime scales are independent per partition, so this pooled test is a
# rough check; the per-partition densities in part 2 are more informative)
wilcox_test <- wilcox.test(pseudotime ~ condition, data = plot_data)

cat("\nWilcoxon test of pseudotime between conditions:\n")
cat("  W statistic:", wilcox_test$statistic, "\n")
cat("  P-value:", format(wilcox_test$p.value, scientific = TRUE), "\n")

# Calculate median pseudotime per condition
median_summary <- plot_data %>%
  group_by(condition) %>%
  summarise(
    median_pseudotime = median(pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_pseudotime = mean(pseudotime, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

cat("\nMedian pseudotime by condition:\n")
print(median_summary)
```

## Branch points and trajectory-associated genes

`graph_test()` computes Moran's I, a measure of spatial autocorrelation, for
each gene on the principal graph; genes with a high value change smoothly along
the trajectory (including across branches). The article runs this test twice
with identical arguments (once under "branch points", once under "genes
correlated with pseudotime"); it is run once here and the result reused.

```{r step6_graph_test}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 16 / STEP 18: Graph test (branch-associated / pseudotime-dependent genes)
#-----------------------------------------------

# FIX: the article calls graph_test() with the same arguments in STEP 16 and
# again in STEP 18; run once and use for both
graph_test_results <- graph_test(
  cds_main,
  neighbor_graph = "principal_graph",
  cores = params$graphtest.cores,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# Identify genes with significant spatial autocorrelation (branch-associated)
sig_genes <- subset(graph_test_results, q_value < params$graphtest.q)

cat("\nGraph test results:\n")
cat("  Total genes tested:", nrow(graph_test_results), "\n")
cat("  Significant genes (q <", params$graphtest.q, "):", nrow(sig_genes), "\n")

if (nrow(sig_genes) > 0) {
  cat("\nTop", params$genes.top_n_branch, "branch-associated genes (by Moran's I):\n")
  top_genes <- head(sig_genes[order(sig_genes$morans_I, decreasing = TRUE), ], params$genes.top_n_branch)
  print(top_genes[, c("gene_short_name", "morans_I", "q_value")])
}
```

## Integrate results back into the Seurat object

```{r step7_to_seurat, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 17: Add pseudotime to Seurat metadata
#-----------------------------------------------

# Create pseudotime vector with cell names (includes all partitions)
pseudotime_vector <- pseudotime(cds_main)
names(pseudotime_vector) <- colnames(cds_main)

# Also add partition information
partition_vector <- partitions(cds_main)
names(partition_vector) <- colnames(cds_main)

# Add to Seurat object
seurat_subset$monocle3_pseudotime <- NA  # Initialize
seurat_subset$monocle3_partition <- NA   # Initialize

seurat_subset$monocle3_pseudotime[colnames(cds_main)] <- pseudotime_vector
seurat_subset$monocle3_partition[colnames(cds_main)] <- as.character(partition_vector)

# Visualize pseudotime in Seurat
p_seurat_pseudotime <- FeaturePlot(
  seurat_subset,
  features = "monocle3_pseudotime",
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  pt.size = 1
) +
  scale_color_viridis(option = "plasma", name = "Pseudotime") +
  ggtitle("Monocle 3 Pseudotime (All Partitions in Seurat)")
print(p_seurat_pseudotime)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/pseudotime/07_pseudotime_in_seurat.png"),
       p_seurat_pseudotime, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

# Also visualize partition assignment
p_seurat_partition <- DimPlot(
  seurat_subset,
  group.by = "monocle3_partition",
  reduction = umap_reduction,
  pt.size = 1
) +
  ggtitle("Monocle 3 Partition Assignment (in Seurat)")
print(p_seurat_partition)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/pseudotime/08_partition_in_seurat.png"),
       p_seurat_partition, width = 10, height = 8, dpi = params$plot.dpi)

# Save updated Seurat object
saveRDS(seurat_subset, file.path(traj.dir, "results/seurat_with_pseudotime.rds"))
```

## Identify genes that change along trajectories

```{r step8_trajectory_genes}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 18: Identify pseudotime-dependent genes
#-----------------------------------------------

# Genes with a significant graph_test result (computed once above; the article
# describes this step as fitting GAMs, but it is the same Moran's I test)
trajectory_genes <- graph_test_results

# Filter for significant genes
sig_trajectory_genes <- subset(trajectory_genes, q_value < params$graphtest.q)

cat("Genes significantly associated with trajectory:\n")
cat("  Total tested:", nrow(trajectory_genes), "\n")
cat("  Significant (q <", params$graphtest.q, "):", nrow(sig_trajectory_genes), "\n")
cat("  Top genes by Moran's I:\n")

# Show top genes
top20_genes <- head(sig_trajectory_genes[order(sig_trajectory_genes$morans_I, decreasing = TRUE), ], params$genes.top_n_table)
print(top20_genes[, c("gene_short_name", "morans_I", "q_value")])

# Save results
write.csv(sig_trajectory_genes,
          file.path(traj.dir, "results/trajectory_associated_genes.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

### Visualize top trajectory genes

```{r step9_top_gene_plots, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 12}
#-----------------------------------------------
# STEP 19: Visualize top trajectory genes
#-----------------------------------------------

# Select top genes for visualization
top_genes_to_plot <- head(top20_genes$gene_short_name, params$genes.top_n_plot)

# Create multi-panel plot
gene_plots <- list()
for (i in 1:length(top_genes_to_plot)) {
  gene <- top_genes_to_plot[i]

  gene_plots[[i]] <- plot_cells(
    cds_main,
    genes = gene,
    label_cell_groups = FALSE,
    show_trajectory_graph = TRUE,
    cell_size = 0.75
  ) +
    scale_color_viridis(option = "magma", name = "Expression") +
    ggtitle(gene) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
          legend.position = "right",
          legend.key.size = unit(0.3, "cm"))
}

# Combine into grid
p_top_genes <- wrap_plots(gene_plots, ncol = 3)
print(p_top_genes)

ggsave(file.path(traj.dir, "plots/genes_over_pseudotime/07_top_trajectory_genes.png"),
       p_top_genes, width = 14, height = 12, dpi = params$plot.dpi)
```

## Common pitfalls: diagnostic checks

Short checks from the article's "common pitfalls" section.

**Pseudotime driven by batch?** A strong correlation of pseudotime with sample
suggests the trajectory reflects batch rather than biology.

```{r step10_pitfall_batch}
# Check if pseudotime correlates with batch
cor.test(plot_data$pseudotime, as.numeric(factor(plot_data$sample)))
```

**Cell cycle?** Only possible if a `Phase` column exists (from Seurat
`CellCycleScoring()`, not run in this series).

```{r step11_pitfall_cellcycle, eval = "Phase" %in% colnames(colData(cds_main))}
# Check cell cycle phase distribution along pseudotime
table(colData(cds_main)$Phase, cut(pseudotime(cds_main), breaks = 5))
```

**Biologically implausible root?** Check that "mature" markers are LOW at
pseudotime = 0, and that the top trajectory genes above are known to be involved
in the process being studied.

**Too many partitions, or pseudotime compared across partitions?**

```{r step12_pitfall_partitions}
# Check number of partitions
length(unique(partitions(cds_main)))

# Check if you're comparing pseudotime across partitions
plot_data %>% group_by(partition) %>% summarise(max_pt = max(pseudotime))
```
